steps.name: destination-roots-realpathed-by-destination
steps.predicate: declared destination roots must equal the DESTINATION's own realpath — adopt refuses otherwise, and the source engine cannot measure another host

steps.name: red-copy-first-adopt-refused
steps.predicate: copy-first is the operator's natural instinct and must fail closed rather than produce an unauthorized live target
steps.bothHalves: the SAME command with the same flags is accepted in the `adopt` stage below, so this refusal measures the ordering rather than a broken invocation

steps.name: carve-outs-still-answer
steps.note: relocation-inspect at the vacated source is one half of the mandated close-out; relocation-abort is the only exit. Both carve-outs are load-bearing, not incidental.

steps.name: per-file-reconciliation-both-directions
steps.predicate: each side computes its own per-file sha256 with its own node; the comparison is full-value and runs in both directions

steps.name: vm-verifies-the-transported-bytes-against-the-vacate-manifest
steps.finding: the vacate is the LAST WRITER of workspace.json, so the plain CLI snapshot-verify can never be green against a vacate-time manifest. It names exactly one file and that is the transport proof; the byte comparison the adopt actually performs excludes that file and is green here.

steps.name: destination-refuses-until-adopted
steps.note: between vacate and adopt ZERO addresses are alive; source and copy refuse with DIFFERENT codes and both are actionable

steps.name: red-dropped-empty-directory
steps.note: without the first half the second would be a check that cannot be shown to measure anything

steps.name: red-wrong-stage-permit
steps.note: same actor, same workspaceId, same destination, same relocationId — only `stage` differs, which is the term that makes the permit per-verb rather than per-hop

steps.name: adopt-is-idempotent
steps.note: a verb that half-applies on retry is the same defect as a torn write

steps.name: vm-validate-and-status
steps.note: relocation transforms no event and advances no version; a head that moved would mean the hop rewrote the chain

steps.name: post-adopt-bytes-still-answer-to-the-vacate-manifest
steps.note: after the adopt EXACTLY ONE control file has legitimately changed — workspace.json, which now carries the relocation ledger — and every other byte still matches what the source signed for at the vacate. The adopt is a binding change, not a chain change

steps.name: red-abort-permit-cannot-be-pre-minted-in-the-vacate-document

selfReference.why: the vacated ledger entry contains authority.authorityFileSha256, and the commitment is sha256 over that entry — so a document carrying a satisfiable abort permit for the hop its own vacate permit authorised would have to contain a digest of itself

steps.ceiling: this is a review device, not a barrier: a SECOND document minted after the vacate satisfies it trivially. What it buys is two documents and two approvals where there was one, and a permanent difference between the two authorityFileSha256 values of an aborted hop

steps.budget: the cap is spent by ATTEMPTS, not by moves: this hop moved zero bytes and cost two of sixteen ledger entries, permanently

processResidue.note: no dev server, tunnel, watcher or headless browser was started by this rehearsal; the check runs anyway

findings.finding: The plain CLI `snapshot-verify` can NEVER be green against a vacate-time control manifest.
findings.why: `relocation-plan`/`relocation-vacate` compute the manifest under the lease BEFORE appending the ledger entry, and appending it rewrites `workspace.json`. The vacate is therefore the last writer of the one file its own manifest describes.
findings.measured: the CLI verb answers SNAPSHOT_MISMATCH naming exactly one file — `workspace.json` — while the engine's own verifySnapshotManifest(..., { excludePaths: ['workspace.json'] }), which is literally the call relocation-adopt makes, answers SNAPSHOT_VERIFIED.
findings.consequenceForTheRunbook: a runbook step that says 'run snapshot-verify after the vacate and expect SNAPSHOT_VERIFIED' would be a step that can only ever fail. State the exclusion, or state that the single named file IS the expected delta.

findings.finding: Copy-first (adopt before vacate) is refused with WORKSPACE_RELOCATION_NOT_PENDING, not with a root-identity error.
findings.why: a pre-vacate copy carries no `relocations` field at all, so `readMetadata`'s relocation admission never runs; adopt then finds no trailing hop.
findings.note: the ordering is enforced, which is what matters — but an operator diagnosing the failure will be told 'nothing to adopt' rather than 'this tree is not bound here', and the runbook should say so.

findings.finding: The relocation authority document's permits must be in the engine's canonical order (`actorId relocationId stage`), or the document is refused as WORKSPACE_RELOCATION_AUTHORITY_MALFORMED before any permit is matched.
findings.measured: a document listing vacate before abort for one hop was refused with reason `permits order`; the same permits sorted admitted cleanly.
findings.consequenceForTheRunbook: mint every authority through the engine's own `canonicalRelocationAuthority` — a hand-written document that looks correct will be rejected on ordering alone.

findings.finding: The ledger cap is spent by ATTEMPTS. The abort drill's hop moved zero bytes and permanently consumed two of sixteen ledger entries.
findings.measured: relocation-inspect reports ledgerEntriesRemaining 14 at the revived source; there is no compaction verb and deliberately will not be one.
findings.consequenceForTheRealHop: the real all-partition relocation must be planned against a budget of eight attempts per workspace, and rehearsals must never be run on the real chains.

ceilings: This mechanism cannot prevent a fork; it can only make one legible at the two addresses its ledger names. Every claim stronger than that is false.

The two-sided close-out proven here is a statement about TWO ADDRESSES ON THE HOSTS WHERE IT RAN, never about the relocationId globally: one adopt permit presented at the same destination path on N hosts yields N live authorities and the close-out passes at every one of them (ADR 0003 ceiling 4).

`workspace.json` is the one part of the control tree the event hash chain does not cover. Anyone with write access to a vacated source can restore its pre-vacate bytes and the address is fully alive again; the engine cannot detect this.

The abort-stage permit and its vacateCommitmentSha256 are a review device, not a barrier: they buy two documents and two approvals where there was one. This rehearsal measured exactly that and claims nothing more.

This rehearsal proves the CEREMONY is executable. It does not authorize the real hop, and it says nothing about a chain whose export exceeds the engine's one-MiB ceiling or whose partitions share the framework and release-trust roots — the OD-D sequencing question is named in ADR 0003 and is not exercised here.
